features/annotate-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Explain the screenshot without a long message

Skreen includes 13 annotation tools for marking up a capture. Use an arrow to point to a control, text to label a state, or a shape to outline a region. Measurement and other marks help with design feedback when the exact position or size matters.

A simple annotation workflow

  1. Capture the relevant area, window, or scrolling page.
  2. Add one or two marks that answer the reader’s first question: where should I look, and what changed?
  3. Keep labels short and use a consistent color when you have several steps.
  4. Check whether the image contains account names, private messages, or credentials. Cover those details before export.

For a bug report, capture the broken state and mark the control or message that triggered it. For a tutorial, use numbered captures in a combined composition when one image cannot show the whole flow.

Keep the original message visible

Annotations should guide attention, not obscure the interface you are trying to show. Crop first, keep marks outside important text where possible, and review the final export at the size your reader will see.

features/beautiful-backgrounds.bodyHtml:
Pick a look that fits the content

Skreen offers 48 curated gradient presets and 13 procedural patterns. You can also use a custom gradient or a desktop wallpaper, including your current wallpaper and installed macOS wallpapers. Auto-Beautify can suggest a treatment based on the colors in your screenshot.

Set up the background

  1. Capture an area or window and open it in the editor.
  2. Choose a background that keeps the screenshot readable. Add a frame or shadow if it helps separate the interface from the background.
  3. Set the aspect ratio for where the image will appear, such as a presentation slide or a social post.
  4. Review the export at its intended size. Skreen can export at the source image’s native pixel density for a sharper result.

A bright background can be useful for product announcements. For dense text, use a quiet color and enough padding so the content remains the focus. You can annotate the same capture before exporting.

Before and after: a release-note image

The raw capture shows a browser or app window edge to edge. For the finished version, place that same capture on a quiet background, add padding around it, and use a restrained frame or shadow to separate the window from the page. Judge legibility in the editor preview before export. Keep small interface text readable at the final size; a decorative background cannot fix an overly reduced capture.

features/combine-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Choose a layout

Use a grid when the images should have equal weight, such as several steps in a workflow. Use Free Canvas when you want to place captures at different sizes or positions. Skreen can add a new capture to an existing composition, so you can build the image as you work.

Build a clear comparison

  1. Capture the first state and add it to a composition.
  2. Capture the next state, or add another existing capture.
  3. Align the images so the reader can compare the same region in each one. Add short annotations to identify the change.
  4. Apply a consistent background and spacing, then export a single image.

If the source images have different sizes, preview the composition at the final display size. Small UI text may become hard to read when several full-screen captures are squeezed into one canvas; crop each frame to the relevant area first.

Example: a two-state bug report

Place a capture of the expected state next to the broken state in a two-column grid. Crop both to the same control, then add a short label above each one. The reader can compare the change without switching between files. If one state needs more room, move the captures to Free Canvas and size them independently. Export the composition as one image only after checking that both labels and the relevant UI are legible.

features/ocr-and-qr.bodyHtml:
Capture text without retyping

Use Skreen’s Capture Text action when the text itself is all you need. You can also recognize text from an image already open in the editor. Recognition uses Apple’s Vision framework on your device.

For example, capture an error message from an app, copy it as text, and paste it into a support ticket. You can still save the image when the visual context matters.

Copy text step by step

  1. Capture the line or open an existing screenshot in Skreen.
  2. Use Capture Text or the editor’s text recognition action.
  3. Compare the recognized text against the image, especially punctuation, numbers, and line breaks.
  4. Copy the text into your document or support ticket. Keep the screenshot with it when the original layout helps explain the problem.

Read a QR code from a capture

Skreen can detect QR codes in captured content. Review the recognized destination before opening or sharing it, just as you would with any link from an unfamiliar source.

For example, if a QR code appears in a presentation slide, capture that region and read the destination in Skreen before deciding whether to visit it. Check the actual URL rather than relying on the surrounding label.

Check the result

OCR accuracy depends on the image. Tiny text, low contrast, unusual fonts, and overlapping UI can produce mistakes. Compare the recognized text with the screenshot before you rely on it for a command, address, or important number. If the image contains private data, redact it before sharing.

features/redact-screenshots.bodyHtml:
Find details before they leave your Mac

Skreen uses Apple Vision on your device to look for faces and sensitive text. Detection covers email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, IP addresses, API keys, passwords, US Social Security numbers, and custom patterns you define. You can also select an area yourself when automatic detection misses something.

How to redact a screenshot

  1. Take a screenshot or open a capture in the Skreen editor.
  2. Run sensitive-data detection and inspect the proposed matches. Add or adjust selections where needed.
  3. Choose blur, pixelation, or a solid cover for each area. Use the manual selection for anything the detector did not identify.
  4. Zoom in and check the full image, including edges and background content, before exporting the file you intend to share.

For text, the Alt key can snap a selection to word boundaries. This makes it easier to cover a single token without hiding the surrounding explanation.

Example: a payment form

Imagine a bug report showing a payment form. In the unedited capture, the field values sit beside the error you need to explain. Cover the card number with a solid block while keeping the form labels and surrounding interface visible. Check the exported file: the private value should be unreadable, and the evidence for the bug should still be clear.

Choose the right cover

Blur or pixelation can make a design review easier to read while obscuring an incidental name or face. For secrets such as passwords, API keys, and payment details, a solid cover is the clearer choice. Automated detection is a helper, so always review the exported image yourself before sharing sensitive material.

features/scrolling-screenshots.bodyHtml:
How to take a scrolling screenshot

  1. Open the page or scrollable view and bring the part you want to capture into view.
  2. Start a scrolling capture in Skreen and select the content area. Keep the selection inside the scrolling region so fixed browser chrome is left out.
  3. Start scrolling. You can pause, change direction, resume, or cancel while capturing. Finish when you have reached the end of the section you need.
  4. Review the stitched image in the editor. Crop extra space, add an annotation, or hide private details before you export.

Skreen combines overlapping frames and works to avoid repeating elements that stay fixed while the content moves.

If macOS asks for Screen Recording access during the first capture, open System Settings, grant Skreen the requested access, and return to the app. macOS may ask you to restart the app before the new permission takes effect. Choose only the content you intend to capture; browser tabs and conversations can include private information outside the visible area.

When it helps

Use scrolling capture for a long article, a support conversation, a design review, a document, or a bug report where the content extends beyond one screen. If you only need what is visible right now, an area or window capture is quicker.

What to check before sharing

Dynamic content can change while a page scrolls. Animations, expanding panels, and lazy-loaded sections may produce a different image from a static page. Keep the view steady, let content load, and review the final stitch before sending it. Scrolling capture works best when the content moves inside a clearly selected scroll area.

Scrolling capture questions

Why is part of the page repeated or missing?

Moving banners, autoplay video, sticky elements, or content that loads during the scroll can interrupt the stitch. Let the page settle, select the actual scrolling region, and try a shorter capture. Inspect the exported image rather than assuming every frame joined cleanly.

Can I capture a long chat or document?

Yes, when its content scrolls inside a selectable region. Start with a short section to confirm the result, then capture the full portion you need. If the view does not scroll consistently, use separate area captures and combine them.

guides/how-to-screenshot-on-mac.bodyHtml:
The built-in Mac screenshot shortcuts

What you want Shortcut What happens
The entire screen Shift–Command–3 macOS captures the screen.
A selected area Shift–Command–4 Drag the crosshair over the area you need.
A window or menu Shift–Command–4, then Space Move the camera over a window and click.
Screenshot controls Shift–Command–5 Open the Screenshot app to choose a capture or recording mode.

These are macOS shortcuts; you can use them without installing Skreen. Apple’s screenshot guide also explains where the resulting files are saved and how the Screenshot app’s options work.

Capture an area in Skreen

Skreen uses Shift–Command–0 by default for area capture. Drag to select what you need, and the screenshot opens in the Skreen editor. The Shift–Command–4 shortcut in the table above belongs to macOS.

If the page is longer than one screen

A standard area or window screenshot captures what is visible. For a long page, document, or scrollable view, use Skreen’s scrolling capture: select the content region, scroll through the part you need, and finish with one stitched image. Check the final image before sharing, especially if the page contains animation or content that loads as you scroll.

Make the screenshot ready to share

Use annotations to point to the relevant button or problem. Add a background when presentation matters. If the capture contains personal information, use redaction and inspect the export. Skreen can also extract text and QR codes from a capture.

If a native macOS shortcut already produces the file you need, you can stop there. Use Skreen when you need the extra capture and editing steps together.

guides/how-to-screenshot-a-whole-webpage.bodyHtml:
Shift–Command–3, Shift–Command–4, and the Screenshot app (Shift–Command–5) capture what is visible on the screen. A long article, a pricing table, or a chat history is usually taller than the window, so you need a different method for the rest of the page.

Safari: export the page as a PDF or capture it in Web Inspector

  1. Open the page and choose File → Export as PDF…. Safari saves the whole page as one PDF.
  2. If you need an image, open the PDF in Preview and choose File → Export…, then pick PNG or JPEG.

For an image that matches the screen layout more closely, turn on Safari → Settings → Advanced → Show features for web developers. Open Web Inspector with Option–Command–I, select the <body> or <html> node in the Elements tab, right-click it, and choose Capture Screenshot.

Chrome, Edge, Arc, and other Chromium browsers

  1. Press Option–Command–I to open Developer Tools.
  2. Press Shift–Command–P to open the command menu and type screenshot.
  3. Choose Capture full size screenshot. The browser saves a PNG of the entire page to your Downloads folder.

Firefox

Right-click an empty part of the page and choose Take Screenshot, or press Shift–Command–S. Click Save full page, then download or copy the image.

What can go wrong with browser captures

  • Lazy-loaded images may appear blank. Scroll to the bottom of the page once before you capture.
  • Infinite feeds have no real end. The browser captures only what has loaded.
  • Scrollable panels inside a page, such as a chat column or a code viewer, are not expanded by full-page capture.
  • Apps outside the browser, such as Slack, Notes, Mail, or Xcode, have no full-page option at all.

A scrolling screenshot of any window with Skreen

Skreen’s scrolling capture works on the region you select, in any app:

  1. Choose Scrolling Capture from the Skreen menu bar icon.
  2. Select the area that scrolls, such as the article column or the message list.
  3. Start the capture. Skreen scrolls the content for you; pause, change direction, or finish when you reach the part you need.
  4. Check the stitched image in the editor before you share it.

Skreen detects the overlap between frames and avoids repeating fixed headers, footers, sidebars, and floating controls. When the image is ready, you can add arrows and notes or cover private details in the same editor.

Which method to use

MethodWorks inResult
Safari Export as PDFSafariPDF of the whole page
Chrome Capture full size screenshotChromium browsersPNG of the whole page
Firefox Save full pageFirefoxPNG of the whole page
Skreen Scrolling CaptureAny app on macOS 14 or laterOne image of the selected scrolling region, ready to edit

Questions

Does macOS have a built-in scrolling screenshot?

The built-in Screenshot tool captures the screen, a window, or a selected area as it appears on screen. For anything taller, use a browser’s full-page option or a scrolling capture tool.

Can I capture a whole page without an extension?

Yes. Safari, Chrome, and Firefox can all do it with the built-in steps above.

guides/how-to-screenshot-a-window-on-mac.bodyHtml:
Capture one window

  1. Press Shift–Command–4. The pointer turns into a crosshair.
  2. Press Space. The pointer turns into a camera and the window under it is highlighted.
  3. Click the window you want. macOS saves the image to the Desktop by default.

The same method works for an open menu. You can also press Shift–Command–5 and click Capture Selected Window in the toolbar.

Remove the window shadow

A window capture includes the window’s drop shadow on a transparent background, which adds empty space around the image. To leave it out for one capture, hold Option while you click the window.

To turn the shadow off for every window capture, run this in Terminal:

defaults write com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow -bool true
killall SystemUIServer

To bring the shadow back:

defaults delete com.apple.screencapture disable-shadow
killall SystemUIServer

Copy to the clipboard instead of saving a file

Add Control to the shortcut: press Control–Shift–Command–4, then Space, then click the window. Paste the image into a chat, an email, or a document with Command–V.

Capture a window in Skreen

In Skreen, choose Capture Window from the menu bar icon. Pick the window with the pointer, or choose it from the list of open windows in the menu. The capture opens in the editor, where you can:

  • place it on a gradient, wallpaper, or solid background with padding, rounded corners, and a shadow you control;
  • point to the important part with arrows, text, and numbered steps;
  • hide names, emails, or tokens before you share it.

Questions

Why does my window screenshot have a big transparent border?

That border is the window shadow. Hold Option when you click, or turn the shadow off with the Terminal command above.

Where did my window screenshot go?

By default, macOS saves screenshots to the Desktop. See how to change where screenshots are saved.

guides/how-to-change-where-screenshots-a.bodyHtml:
Choose a folder in the Screenshot app

  1. Press Shift–Command–5 to open the Screenshot toolbar.
  2. Click Options.
  3. Under Save to, choose Desktop, Documents, Clipboard, Mail, Messages, or Preview, or pick Other Location… and select a folder.

The setting applies to every shortcut, including Shift–Command–3 and Shift–Command–4. Create a dedicated folder first, for example Pictures/Screenshots, so captures do not mix with other files.

Set the folder with Terminal

If you prefer a command, create the folder and point macOS to it:

mkdir -p ~/Pictures/Screenshots
defaults write com.apple.screencapture location ~/Pictures/Screenshots
killall SystemUIServer

To go back to the Desktop:

defaults delete com.apple.screencapture location
killall SystemUIServer

Skip the file and copy to the clipboard

Add Control to any screenshot shortcut, for example Control–Shift–Command–4. macOS copies the image instead of saving a file, and you paste it with Command–V. You can also choose Clipboard under Save to to make this the default.

Change the file format

macOS saves screenshots as PNG. To save JPEG files instead, run:

defaults write com.apple.screencapture type jpg
killall SystemUIServer

Replace jpg with png to switch back.

Find screenshots you cannot locate

Open Shift–Command–5 → Options to see where captures go now. To list every screenshot on your Mac, search in Finder or Spotlight for kMDItemIsScreenCapture:1.

Where Skreen saves images

Skreen keeps the macOS setting untouched. Edited images are saved to the folder chosen in Skreen Settings → Export, which is your Downloads folder until you pick another one. You can also copy the finished image, drag it straight into another app, or reopen earlier captures from the editor’s history.

guides/how-to-copy-text-from-an-image-on.bodyHtml:
Use Live Text in Preview, Photos, and Safari

On macOS Monterey and later, Live Text recognizes text in images:

  1. Open the image or screenshot in Preview or Photos, or find it on a web page in Safari.
  2. Move the pointer over the text until it changes to a text cursor.
  3. Drag to select the words and press Command–C.

You can also press Space on an image in Finder to open Quick Look and select text there. If text cannot be selected, check that Live Text is turned on in System Settings → General → Language & Region.

Copy text that is only on the screen

Live Text works on images you open. Text in a video, a remote desktop session, an error dialog, or a locked PDF must be captured first. The usual route is to take a screenshot, open it in Preview, and select the text. Skreen shortens this to one action:

  1. Choose Capture Text from the Skreen menu bar icon.
  2. Select the area that contains the text or a QR code.
  3. Skreen recognizes the text on your Mac with Apple Vision and shows it in a small result panel. Copy what you need.

Nothing is uploaded: recognition runs on your Mac. If you already have a capture open in the editor, use Text & QR to read the current image.

Read a QR code on the screen

A QR code on a web page or in a presentation can be read the same way. Select it with Capture Text, and Skreen shows the decoded payload, such as a link or Wi-Fi details, so you can copy it without reaching for your phone.

Get cleaner results

  • Capture only the text you need. Smaller selections avoid stray words from toolbars and sidebars.
  • Zoom in on small or low-contrast text before capturing.
  • Review numbers, codes, and passwords character by character. Similar shapes such as 0 and O can be confused.
  • Handwriting and stylized fonts are recognized less reliably than printed text.

guides/best-screenshot-app-for-mac.bodyHtml:
Most people need three things from a screenshot tool: capture the right part of the screen, explain it with a mark or two, and share it without leaking private details. Here is how the main Mac options handle that. Features were checked in November 2026; prices change, so confirm them on each developer’s site.

At a glance

macOS ScreenshotSkreenCleanShot XShottrSnagit
Area, window, full screenYesYesYesYesYes
Scrolling captureNoYesYesYesYes
AnnotationsBasic MarkupYesYesYesYes
Text recognition (OCR)Live Text in opened imagesYes, plus QRYesYesYes
Automatic detection of private dataNoYes, on deviceManual blur and pixelateManualManual
Backgrounds and framingNoYesYesBasicEffects
Screen recordingYesNoYesNoYes
Cloud share linksNoNoYesLimitedYes
PlatformsmacOSmacOS 14+macOSmacOSmacOS and Windows
Price modelIncludedFree during public betaPaid license, optional cloud planFree to try, paid licenseSubscription

macOS Screenshot: enough for quick captures

The built-in tool (Shift–Command–3, 4, and 5) captures the screen, an area, or a window, records video, and offers basic Markup from the floating thumbnail. It is the right choice when you only need the file. It has no scrolling capture and no tools for backgrounds or automatic redaction. See how to take a screenshot on Mac.

Skreen: capture, explain, and protect in one editor

Skreen is a menu bar app for macOS 14 and later. It captures an area, a window, the full screen, a repeated area, a timed capture, or a scrolling region. The editor has arrows, text, shapes, numbered steps, a magnifier, and stickers. It can combine several screenshots in a grid or on a free canvas, add backgrounds, and read text and QR codes.

Its distinctive feature is on-device detection of faces, emails, phone numbers, card numbers, API keys, passwords, and custom patterns, which you review before export. Choose Skreen if you share screenshots of real work and want to explain them and protect data in one place. It does not record video or upload to a cloud.

CleanShot X: the broadest feature set

CleanShot X covers screenshots, scrolling capture, screen recording with GIF export, annotation, a background tool, text recognition, and cloud share links. It is a mature paid app, also available through Setapp. Choose it if you record video as often as you take screenshots or rely on share links. See how Skreen compares with CleanShot X.

Shottr: small and fast

Shottr is a lightweight capture tool with scrolling capture, OCR, annotation, and pixel-level tools such as a ruler and color picker that designers and developers like. It does not record video. Choose it if you want a minimal utility and precise measurement.

Snagit: for teams on Mac and Windows

Snagit from TechSmith captures images and video on both macOS and Windows and includes templates for step-by-step guides. It is sold as a subscription. Choose it if your team documents processes across both platforms.

How to choose

  • You just need a file: the built-in macOS tool.
  • You share screenshots that may contain private data: Skreen.
  • You record screen videos and share links: CleanShot X.
  • You want a tiny utility with pixel tools: Shottr.
  • Your team works on Mac and Windows: Snagit.

guides/cleanshot-x-alternative.bodyHtml:
CleanShot X is a popular paid screenshot and screen recording app for Mac. If you mostly take screenshots and want a different approach to editing and privacy, Skreen is an alternative worth trying. We make Skreen, so the comparison below also lists what CleanShot X does and Skreen does not. Features were checked in November 2026.

Side by side

SkreenCleanShot X
Area, window, full screen, timerYesYes
Repeat the last areaYesYes
Scrolling captureYes, with pause and direction controlYes
Annotation toolsArrows, text, shapes, steps, magnifier, ruler, stickersArrows, text, shapes, steps, highlights
Automatic detection of private dataFaces, emails, phones, cards, API keys, passwords, custom patternsManual blur and pixelate
Combine screenshotsGrid and free canvasNot a core feature
BackgroundsGradients, patterns, wallpapers, Auto-BeautifyBackground tool
Text recognitionText and QR codes, on deviceText
Code imagesYesNo
Screen recording and GIFNoYes
Cloud share linksNoYes
PriceFree during public betaPaid license, optional cloud plan

Where Skreen is different

Private data is found for you

Skreen uses Apple Vision on your Mac to find faces and sensitive text in a screenshot: email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, IP addresses, API keys, passwords, and your own regular expressions. You review each match and choose blur, pixelation, or a solid cover. Learn how redaction works.

Several screenshots become one image

Capture a few screens, then arrange them in a grid or on a free canvas inside the same editor. This helps with before-and-after comparisons and step-by-step bug reports.

Screenshots and code share one editor

Paste code, pick one of 21 languages and 10 themes, and export a styled code image next to your screenshots.

Where CleanShot X is the better choice

  • Screen recording. Skreen does not record video or GIFs.
  • Share links. CleanShot Cloud uploads a capture and gives you a link; Skreen keeps everything on your Mac.
  • Maturity. CleanShot X has been on the market for years and is available through Setapp. Skreen is in public beta.
  • Older macOS. Skreen requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later.

Switching to Skreen

  1. Download Skreen and move it to Applications. It lives in the menu bar.
  2. Skreen captures an area with Shift–Command–0 by default, so it does not take over the macOS or CleanShot shortcuts. You can remap every capture shortcut in Settings.
  3. Try a scrolling capture and run sensitive-data detection on a real screenshot to see whether the workflow suits you.

Both apps can be installed side by side, so you can compare them on your own work before deciding.

faq.question: Can Skreen capture a page that is longer than my screen?
faq.answer: Yes. Select the scrollable area, scroll through the content you need, then review the stitched image before exporting it.

faq.question: Are my screenshots uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Captures, editing, text recognition, and sensitive-data detection run on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I combine several screenshots into one image?
faq.answer: Yes. Arrange captures in a grid or freely on a canvas, then export the finished composition.

faq.question: Can I copy text from a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. Skreen recognizes text in images on your Mac so you can copy the words you need.

faq.question: Can I change the background of a screenshot?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a Mac wallpaper, a solid color, or a custom gradient, then adjust the spacing and frame in the editor.

faq.question: What version of macOS do I need?
faq.answer: Skreen requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
